LESSON: PATTERNS CLASSIFICATION

Grade: PP1
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Patterns CLASSIFICATION

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Patterns CLASSIFICATION. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify similarities in patterns in • A few

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: PATTERNS CLASSIFICATION
Patterns CLASSIFICATION is a Grade mathematics skill used at school, at the market, and at home.

HOW TO STUDY THIS TOPIC
1. Read each idea slowly.
2. Copy every worked example into your book and recalculate it yourself.
3. Then try the practice questions without looking at the answers.

WORKED EXAMPLE STYLE
Write the question clearly. Show each step. Box the final answer.
Example framework:
  Question: (write a Patterns CLASSIFICATION problem)
  Step 1: …
  Step 2: …
  Answer: …

KENYAN CONTEXT
Use shillings, market goods, school desks, or garden plots as story numbers so the maths feels real.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Solve one simple Patterns CLASSIFICATION question using objects or a drawing.

Example 2: Solve a harder Patterns CLASSIFICATION question showing every step.

Example 3: Make a word problem about Patterns CLASSIFICATION set at a Kenyan market.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write and solve five questions on Patterns CLASSIFICATION.
2. Explain one solution aloud to a parent or friend.
3. Invent one new word problem and solve it.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Complete 10 practice questions on Patterns CLASSIFICATION in your exercise book.
2. Mark your work. Redo any question you missed.
3. Teach a younger learner one method from this lesson.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify similarities in patterns in • A few

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
